# crispyx

> crispyx runs quality control, normalisation, pseudo-bulk aggregation,
> differential expression, control checks and PCA/KNN on CRISPR and
> Perturb-seq screens stored as .h5ad files, streaming from disk under a
> memory budget so that million-cell screens run on a laptop or a cluster
> node. The API mirrors Scanpy.

## Purpose

crispyx solves a specific problem: genome-wide CRISPR screens produce datasets
with hundreds of thousands to millions of cells. Standard tools (Scanpy,
Pertpy) load the full count matrix into RAM, requiring 30–120 GB or more.
crispyx streams directly from .h5ad files on disk so that quality control,
normalization, pseudobulk aggregation, and differential expression all run
without materializing the full matrix.

## Key capabilities

- Streaming QC and preprocessing (filter cells, perturbations, genes;
  normalize and log-transform; subsample; thin counts) without loading the
  full matrix
- Data preparation: edit obs/var without reading X; normalise perturbation
  labels and take target genes out of guide names; assign guides from
  guide-capture counts; recover integer counts from log1p-normalised data;
  sum the rows of a gene split over several (cx.pp.collapse_genes);
  concatenate multi-file screens; check a file for the mistakes that mislead
  an analysis (cx.pp.check_data)
- Pseudobulk aggregation: average log expression and pseudobulk count matrices
- Differential expression: t-test, Wilcoxon rank-sum (also batch-stratified),
  negative binomial GLM at cell level or on pseudo-bulk with covariates and
  apeGLM log-fold-change shrinkage; a fixed-offset NB test for many small
  perturbations against a large, stratified control set
  (cx.tl.nb_offset_test); covariate-adjusted residual effects
- Control checks: do the control guides agree, and may unassigned cells join
  the controls?
- Memory-efficient PCA and KNN graph construction on backed AnnData
- Scanpy-compatible API: cx.pp, cx.pb, cx.tl, cx.pl namespaces
- HPC support: resume/checkpoint, configurable memory_limit_gb, Docker and
  Singularity images

## Intended users

Computational biologists analyzing large-scale CRISPR or Perturb-seq datasets
who cannot load the full count matrix into memory, or who work on HPC systems
with per-job memory limits. Also useful for anyone running multiple DE methods
at scale (t-test, Wilcoxon, NB-GLM) on the same dataset.

## Relationship to other tools

- **vs Scanpy**: crispyx uses the same AnnData-based API and produces
  identical results (Pearson r > 0.9999 for t-test and Wilcoxon), but uses
  2–43x less time and 2–6x less memory by streaming from disk rather than
  loading into RAM.
- **vs Pertpy/PyDESeq2**: crispyx's NB-GLM fits DESeq2's model per
  perturbation against the controls, streamed under a memory budget; given
  the same size factors and mean floor, z correlation 0.997-0.9999 with
  PyDESeq2. It completes genome-wide screens where Pertpy/PyDESeq2 exceeds
  the available memory.
- **vs edgeR**: edgeR times out or errors on most genome-wide datasets tested.
  crispyx completes all 12 benchmark datasets.

## Benchmarks

Benchmarked across 12 public CRISPR screen datasets (21K–1.97M cells):
- crispyx completes all 12 datasets; Scanpy times out or OOMs on large screens;
  Pertpy and edgeR fail on most genome-wide datasets.
- t-test: 2–11x faster than Scanpy with identical results
- Wilcoxon: 2–43x faster than Scanpy with identical results
- NB-GLM: completes where Pertpy/PyDESeq2 runs out of memory; one
  perturbation against 535,000 control cells with 147 coefficients takes
  33 minutes on 32 cores
